audit.whatIsWrong: Every mention on both layers spells the ability 'Beartrap on a Rope'. The ability is Bear Trap on a Rope. The page also treats it as an instant pull.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kled throws a bear trap that damages and hooks an enemy champion. If SHACKLED FOR A SHORT DURATION, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled.' The hook lands first and the yank only happens if you are still shackled when the timer expires — so walking out of the shackle range before it completes cancels the pull and the bonus damage entirely. That is the counterplay to his only engage, and it was not on the page.
audit.corrected: Name fixed to Bear Trap on a Rope in every touched field including focus.text; the shackle-then-yank timing and the walk-out counterplay written into the early text, mid, wants.you, the do's and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Skaarl is mentioned only as 'remounting Skaarl restores his full dueling kit'. Pocket Pistol is never named, and neither is the damage penalty.
audit.why: Riot: while dismounted 'Kled's abilities change and he deals LESS damage to champions', his Q becomes Pocket Pistol — a ranged blast that knocks Kled backwards and restores courage — and 'Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by FIGHTING ENEMIES', remounting at max courage with a portion of Skaarl's health. So dismounting him is the win, but continuing to brawl him is exactly how he pays for the remount, and his dismounted Q self-knockbacks him out of your 275 taunt range.
audit.corrected: Dismount state written into the level-3 spike, the mid text, whys[3] and the late text: dismount him, then disengage rather than feed courage; Pocket Pistol named with its self-knockback.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly frames the punish as catching 'a Kled who over-commits' with Jousting.
audit.why: Jousting is recastable — 'Kled can cast this ability again to dash back through his initial target.' He is never committed after the first dash, so waiting for an overcommit is waiting for something he chooses not to give. The real window is the 11s Bear Trap and the 13s Jousting both being spent, not a positioning error.
audit.corrected: Reworded across the level-3 spike, mid, whys[2] and the trading rules to key off both cooldowns rather than an imagined overcommit.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere despite 'track it before every punch' being repeated nine times.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7, Jousting 13/12/11/10/9, Chaaaaaaaarge!!! 140/125/110 at 3500-4500 range. His whole kit also costs zero — he pays Courage, not mana — so there is no resource window to wait for, only cooldowns.
audit.corrected: 11s trap, 13s Jousting, 140s ult and the zero-cost note written into the cooldown block, do's line, trading rules and the loading tip.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math' and the loading tip repeats 'Anti-heal if he sustains'.
audit.why: Kled has no heal in his kit — no heal flag on any ability. What he has is a remount that restores a portion of Skaarl's health once courage is full. Grievous Wounds is not the answer to a remount, and telling a Galio to buy an Orb here spends gold on nothing.
audit.corrected: Orb line replaced with the armour-and-HP direction his all-physical kit actually calls for; loading tip replaced with the shackle rule.

edits.before: Kled owns the very start — he has Beartrap on a Rope and chaotic mounted aggression at level 1 while you hold only Winds of War and zero engage, so do not contest the first wave. Last-hit at the tip of your Q tornado and respect the pull; if his Beartrap lands he yanks you in for a free dismounted trade. The lane only evens at Level 3 once Shield of Durand and Justice Punch are both up — and even then your W's anti-magic bonus is wasted on his fully physical kit, so you have to win on the taunt-knockup punish, not on sponging his damage.
edits.after: Kled owns the very start — he has Bear Trap on a Rope and chaotic mounted aggression at level 1 while you hold only Winds of War and zero engage, so do not contest the first wave. Last-hit at the tip of your tornado and respect the hook, but know how it works: the trap shackles first, and only if you are still shackled when the timer runs out does it yank you in for bonus damage. Walk out and the pull never happens. The lane evens at level 3 — and even then your W’s anti-magic bonus is wasted on his physical kit, so you win on the taunt-knockup, not on sponging.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay a coinflip — you trade back only when his Beartrap on a Rope is down, channelling Shield of Durand to eat his dismount burst then releasing the taunt into a Justice Punch knockup. Never throw the E first: its brief wind-up is readable and he'll pull or skirmish you while it's on cooldown. Level 6 is your one clear spike: Hero's Entrance either drops the taunt-knockup onto his committed Chaaaaaaaarge!!! all-in for a kill, or you shove and fly to another lane — make the map your win condition instead of this stubborn 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay a coinflip. Trade back only with his 11s Bear Trap spent AND his 13s Jousting gone, because Jousting recasts straight back through you — he is never actually committed. Charge Shield of Durand to eat the burst, release the taunt, punch the knockup. If you do dismount him, that is the win: dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions, but he restores courage by fighting, so disengage instead of brawling him back onto Skaarl. Level 6 is your clear spike — the landing taunt-knockup answers his 140s Chaaaaaaaarge!!!, or you shove and fly elsewhere.

edits.before: This is where Kled reclaims the lane — once he can reliably remount Skaarl his full dueling kit comes back and his sustained physical damage out-stats your extended trades as your tank-AP scaling plateaus. Don't solo-duel a fed Kled in the sidelane; his kit ignores your W's anti-magic amplification and his remount tempo outlasts your cooldowns. Lean on what you actually do better: Hero's Entrance map presence, peeling carries with the W-taunt, and turning his Chaaaaaaaarge!!! dive onto your team into a multi-man knockup. Win the map, not the matchup.
edits.after: This is where Kled reclaims the lane — courage comes from fighting, so every skirmish he survives buys the remount that hands his full kit back, and his sustained physical damage out-stats you as your tank-AP scaling plateaus. Don't solo-duel a fed Kled in the sidelane; his kit ignores your W's amplification and Pocket Pistol knocks him out of your 275 taunt while he reloads courage. Lean on what you do better: Hero's Entrance map presence, taunt-peel for carries, and turning his Chaaaaaaaarge!!! dive into a multi-man knockup. Win the map.

notes: Name error fixed: the whole page wrote 'Beartrap on a Rope'; the ability is Bear Trap on a Rope. More useful, the mechanic was wrong too — Riot's text is 'If SHACKLED FOR A SHORT DURATION, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled', so the hook lands first and walking out of the shackle before the timer expires cancels both the pull and the bonus damage. That is the counterplay to his only engage and it was missing. Second: the page kept telling the reader to punish 'a Kled who over-commits' with Jousting, but Jousting recasts back through the target, so he is never committed — the window is both cooldowns spent (11s trap, 13s Jousting), not a positioning mistake. Third: the dismount state was never explained. Dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions and his Q becomes Pocket Pistol, which knocks him backwards out of your 275 taunt range — but 'Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by fighting enemies', so continuing to brawl a dismounted Kled is how he pays for the remount. Disengage instead. Fourth: I removed the Oblivion Orb recommendation. Kled has no heal on any ability; the remount restores Skaarl's health, and whether Grievous Wounds touches that is not something the kit file answers, so I redirected the gold to armour and HP rather than assert either way.
